problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
